'''Robert Byron Bird''' (February 5, 1924 – November 13, 2020) was an American chemical engineer and professor emeritus in the department of chemical engineering at the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]]. He was known for his research in [[transport phenomena]] of [[non-Newtonian fluid]]s, including fluid dynamics of [[polymer]]s, polymer kinetic theory, and [[rheology]].<ref name="uwm">{{cite web|url=http://www.engr.wisc.edu/che/faculty/bird_byron.html|title=R. Byron Bird|publisher=[[University of Wisconsin-Madison]]|access-date=2009-11-04}}</ref> He, along with Warren E. Stewart and [[Edwin N. Lightfoot]], was an author of the classic textbook [[Transport Phenomena (book)|Transport Phenomena]].<ref name="garfield">{{cite web|url=https://garfield.library.upenn.edu/classics1979/A1979HJ87300001.pdf|title=This Week's Citation Classic|date=1979-09-17|publisher=garfield.library.upenn.edu|access-date=2009-11-04|archive-date=2018-09-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180920180945/http://www.garfield.library.upenn.edu/classics1979/A1979HJ87300001.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> Bird was a recipient of the [[National Medal of Science]] in 1987.<ref name="nsf">{{cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/od/nms/recip_details.cfm?recip_id=44|title=The President's National Medal of Science: Recipient Details|publisher=[[National Science Foundation]]|access-date=2009-11-04}}</ref>

==Childhood and education==
Robert Byron Bird  was  born  on  February 5, 1924, in Bryan, Texas. His father, Byron Bird, was a professor of civil engineering at [[Texas A&M University]]. In his,<ref>2010 account of his early years</ref><ref name="birdbio">{{cite journal|doi=10.1146/annurev-chembioeng-073009-100922|title=Chemical Engineering Education: A Gallimaufry of Thoughts|year=2010|last1=Bird|first1=R. Byron|journal=Annual Review of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering|volume=1|pages=1–17|pmid=22432570|doi-access=free}}</ref> Bird recounts he obtain his elementary and junior high education in Fort Dodge, Iowa, and thereafter he attending Central High school in Washington D. C. Bird attended [[University of Maryland]] from 1941 to 1943, where he was initiated into the Alpha Rho chapter of [[Alpha Chi Sigma]] in 1943.<ref name="alphachisigma.org">{{cite web | title=Alpha Chi Sigma Fraternity | website=Alpha Chi Sigma | url=http://www.alphachisigma.org/page.aspx?pid=268 | access-date=19 November 2020}}</ref> He had to discontinue his studies during [[World War II]], in which he served in the [[US Army]].<ref name="OH">{{cite web|author=Center for Oral History| title= R. Byron Bird |url=https://oh.sciencehistory.org/oral-histories/bird-r-byron|website= [[Science History Institute]] }}</ref><ref name="transcript">{{cite book|first=James G. |last=Traynham |title=R. Byron Bird, Transcript of an Interview Conducted by James G. Traynham at Madison, Wisconsin on 1 October 1998 |date=1 October 1998 |access-date=27 March 2018 |url=https://oh.sciencehistory.org/sites/default/files/bird_rb_0173_suppl.pdf |place=Philadelphia, PA|publisher=[[Science History Institute|Chemical Heritage Foundation]] }}</ref> As a second lieutenant in the 90th Chemical Mortar Battalion, he saw action from the eastern Belgium to the Austrian border.
Bird received his B.S. degree in [[chemical engineering]] from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] in 1947 and Ph.D. degree in [[physical chemistry]] from [[University of Wisconsin-Madison|University of Wisconsin]] in 1950. During 1950–1951, he was a [[Postdoctoral research|postdoctoral fellow]] at Instituut voor Theoretische Fysica, [[University of Amsterdam|Universiteit van Amsterdam]] under [[Jan Hendrik de Boer|Jan Hendrik de Boer]]. During his postdoc, he co-authored his first textbook, the 1,200-page [[Molecular Theory of Gases and Liquids]], along with his advisor [[Joseph O. Hirschfelder]] and another UW-Madison professor [[Charles F. Curtiss]].

==Awards and honors==
Bird was a recipient of the [[National Medal of Science]]; the Medal was awarded by President [[Ronald Reagan]] "for his profoundly influential books and research on kinetic theory, transport phenomena, the behavior of polymeric fluids, and foreign language study for engineers and scientists."<ref name="nsf" /> He was awarded the [[Bingham Medal]] in 1974 for his outstanding contributions to the field of [[rheology]]<ref name="sor">{{cite web|url=http://www.rheology.org/SoR/awards/Bingham/default.htm|title=Bingham Medalists|publisher=The Society of Rheology |access-date=2009-11-14}}</ref> and [[Eringen Medal]] in 1983.<ref name=SES>{{cite web|title=SES MEDALISTS|url=http://ses.egr.uh.edu/node/12|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151008053312/http://ses.egr.uh.edu/node/12|archive-date=2015-10-08}}</ref>

He was a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] since 1969, member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] since 1989, and a number of foreign academies, including the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1985),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/3874 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811162606/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/3874 |title=Byron Bird |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |archive-date=11 August 2020}}</ref> [[The Royal Academies for Science and the Arts of Belgium|Royal Belgian Academy of Sciences]] (1994). Bird was also a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] since 1981,<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780–2010: Chapter B|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterB.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=July 26, 2011}}</ref> the [[American Physical Society]] since 1970, and the American Academy of Mechanics since 1983. In 2015 he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].

In 2004, Bird was granted the Dutch title Knight of the [[Order of Orange-Nassau]] for his "exceptional contributions to the promotion of Dutch language and culture in the United States and at the University of Wisconsin".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.engr.wisc.edu/che/newsletter/2004_winter/Article04_bird.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040328124559/http://www.engr.wisc.edu/che/newsletter/2004_winter/Article04_bird.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2004-03-28|title=Just call him Sir Bob}}</ref>

He was inducted into the [[Alpha Chi Sigma]] Hall of Fame in 2008.<ref name="alphachisigma.org"/> He was recipient of the [[Reed M. Izatt]] and James J. Christensen Lectureship in 2010.

Bird died in November 2020 at the age of 96.<ref>{{cite web | title=Chemical engineering pioneer Robert Byron Bird passes away at 96 - University of Wisconsin-Madison | website=College of Engineering - University of Wisconsin-Madison | date=17 November 2020 | url=https://www.engr.wisc.edu/news/chemical-engineering-pioneer-robert-byron-bird-passes-away-at-96/ | access-date=19 November 2020}}</ref>

==Books==
Bird was the coauthor of several influential books in [[transport phenomena]] and [[rheology]], including the classic textbook [[Transport Phenomena (book)|''Transport Phenomena'']], which was translated into many foreign languages, including Spanish, Italian, Czech, Russian, Persian, and Chinese and the 1200-page tome ''Molecular Theory of Gases and Liquids''.

* {{cite book | title=TRANSPORT PHENOMENA (2nd Ed.) | publisher=Wiley India Pvt. Limited | year=2006 | isbn=978-81-265-0808-2 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MQ9dyCkcUwEC}}
* {{cite book | last1=Bird | first1=R.B. | last2=Stewart | first2=W.E. | last3=Lightfoot | first3=E.N. | last4=Klingenberg | first4=D.J. | title=Introductory Transport Phenomena | publisher=Wiley | year=2015 | isbn=978-1-118-95371-6 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wwXYBgAAQBAJ}}
* {{cite book | last=Hirschfelder | first=J.O. | title=Molecular theory of gases and liquids, by J.O. Hirschfelder, C.F. Curtiss and R.B. Bird | publisher=publisher not identified | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Yn9inQEACAAJ}}
* {{cite book | last1=Bird | first1=R.B. | last2=Armstrong | first2=R.C. | last3=Hassager | first3=O. | title=Dynamics of Polymeric Liquids, Volume 1: Fluid Mechanics | publisher=Wiley | series=Dynamics of Polymeric Liquids | year=1987 | isbn=978-0-471-80245-7 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=posvAQAAIAAJ}}
*''Dynamics of Polymeric Liquids'', Vol. 2, ''Kinetic Theory'', with C. F. Curtiss, R. C. Armstrong, and O. Hassager, Wiley, (1977, 2nd ed. 1987).

Since the publication of [[Transport Phenomena (book)|''Transport Phenomena'']], the subject of transport phenomena has become a standard and essential course in chemical engineering curricula in universities in the U.S. and abroad.<ref name="alphachisigma.org"/>
